messages:
megan: Hey team — getting a cryptic error from the rerank endpoint when we try to score ~120 docs. API responds with `413` and the message just says "payload too large". Payload size in bytes is ~1.6MB so not sure why. anyone seen this?

jay: Sorry you're hitting this, can you share the exact request that fails (headers + counts)? also which model / endpoint (rerank vs relevance) are you calling?

megan: We're calling POST /v1/rerank (model: redwood-small-ranker) with a query that's ~2.4k chars and docs array of 120 items, average doc length ~600 chars. We don't include embeddings, just raw passages. Here's a minimal repro (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"query":"<~2400 chars>","documents":["<600char doc 1>","<600char doc 2>",... 120 items]}'
```

megan: Response: HTTP/1.1 413
{
  "error": "payload too large",
  "details": "payload exceeds limit"
}

jay: ok thanks. two things to call out: 1) rerank counts tokens across both query + all documents; 2) our current limit is a combined token/char ceiling (server-side) with an older generic 413 message. That message is not helpful, we'll improve it.

jay: For immediate workaround: try either chunking the doc set into multiple smaller rerank calls (e.g., batches of 20-30 docs) or truncate long docs and re-run. If you can, switch to the relevance endpoint which accepts larger doc sets and returns scores suitable for prefiltering, then rerank only the top N.

megan: Truncating is annoying for us because we need full context. If we rerank in chunks, how do we maintain stable ordering across batches?

luca: For deterministic ordering across batches you can: 1) call relevance or a cheap embed-based filter to pick top ~200 candidates; 2) rerank those in a single call if under token limit, else chunk and attach batch-order metadata then merge by score with tie-breaker on original retrieval rank. Not ideal but works.

megan: Can you confirm the exact token/char limits so we can implement safe client-side checks before calling? The docs page only mentions a generic limit.

jay: Current enforcement is: combined token-equivalent cap ~120k tokens (estimate), and a hard payload byte limit around 2MB for the rerank endpoint. Both vary by model family. I'll file an internal note to add per-model limits to the docs and a better 413 body that returns `"error": "input_too_large", "limit_type": "tokens", "limit": "120000", "actual": "..."`.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-3881 created and assigned to eng-runtime; priority: P2.

jay: In the short term I'll paste a tiny client-side validator snippet (javascript) that we recommend:

```js
// rough char->token estimator (fast):
function estTokens(text){ return Math.ceil(text.length / 4); } // conservative
function validateRerank(query, docs){
  let tokens = estTokens(query);
  for(const d of docs) tokens += estTokens(d);
  if(tokens > 120000) return {ok:false,reason:'token_limit',tokens};
  if(JSON.stringify({query,docs}).length > 2000000) return {ok:false,reason:'byte_limit'};
  return {ok:true,tokens};
}
```

megan: That helps, thanks. Can you also escalate to get clearer error messages? This tripped our production monitoring.

jay: Yep — escalated to eng-runtime. Luca, can you look at whether we can change the API to return a structured error now (instead of generic 413)? tagging you for FYI.

luca: Got it. I'll add a short-term change to return structured JSON for payload limits and log the failing request size + token estimate to the request traces. Will aim for a rollout in the next canary.

megan: Appreciate it. We'll implement client-side validator and batch logic tomorrow and test.

jay: Thanks, leaving this thread open. I'll post the bug number and timeline once eng confirms. :thumbsup:
